newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Nov 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Nov 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates' press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Labour contracts and other labour and social affairs ministry documents are to be written in English and Arabic before the end of the year so non-Arab expatriates know what documents they are signing.
- Saudi Arabia pledged its determination to preserve GCC cohesiveness despite Bahrain's threat to boycott next month's GCC summit in Qatar.
- Lull hits real estate sector. The slow cycle of business will affect the lower end of the market, experts said.
- Canada is set to boost businesss ties with the UAE, with a focus on oil, gas, defence and argiculture, a Canadian government official said.
- India became the third biggest exporter to the UAE in the first quarter of 1996, the Dubai Chamber of Commerce and Industry said.
- Oman said it would set up a council shortly to widen the process of consultation in the country.
- Qatar is planing to introduce new laws to make its business law more compatible with international standards, the country's emir said.
- The UAE's cabinet approved a memorandum of the Ministry of Planning for a power grid for the west coast costing 174 million dirhams.
- The Ministry of Labour proposed including 2.3 billion dirhams in spending on new public housing in the budget for the coming year.
- The central bank's foreign currency reserves stood at 27.3 billion dirhams in October. REUTERS
